<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport), syncSchemasBatch (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport), set_column_default (literal, a string literal in diffManagedTable))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c5757e69f506325c7984ee5d1e8d63203e777a37` — the merge of head `835c89dffd8976c5d44442a54c8785e1952e5464` into base `4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c5757e69f506325c7984ee5d1e8d63203e777a37 && git checkout c5757e69f506325c7984ee5d1e8d63203e777a37
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3 835c89dffd8976c5d44442a54c8785e1952e5464 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3 && git merge --no-ff 835c89dffd8976c5d44442a54c8785e1952e5464

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4925039a7558d6477323eeef7b1b16d89da01cc3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f83ae7cf7ea0ff4e9d2adfa6a5d7a66547cab0dc`
Local-runs: none

Review of PR #37469 (card #37413), declaration face. Read: the card body and all five comments (triage 7181830348, claim 7183611467, scope amendment 7183761626, os-dev-report 7184726397, regrade 7185173106), the PR body, final-head comment 7185279058, the net diff `origin/main...pr-37469` (10 files, +357 −75), the check-runs on this head (53 completed: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure; `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core` 1–10, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` green), and for precedent PR #37425 (records 7182460866 and 7183095333) and cards #37430 and #37434. Code outside the diff was read, never reviewed. Nothing was built or run; the dev's test counts and four ablations are taken from the PR body as reported, not re-measured.

### ① Derived judgments

- **A1. The route is the one the scope amendment orders, and the diff follows it.** Column added nullable with no DEFAULT (`withholdsNowDefault` in `createColumn` and in `columnDeclarationSQL`, NOT NULL and DEFAULT withheld together), one `UPDATE` after the `ADD COLUMN`, drift reports `set_column_default` plus `tighten_not_null`, local ceremony rebuild imposes both, remote answers `needs-table-rebuild`. `storage.notNull` is never dropped silently: the differ reports it. The remote-only copy `declaresNowColumnDefault` is deleted and both faces ask `declaresSqliteNowColumnDefault`; no second copy remains.
- **A2. The backfill value is the DEFAULT's own expression.** `sqliteNowBackfillSql` sets each column to `sqliteNowColumnDefaultSql(String(field.type || 'string'))`, the same function with the same type string that `sqliteDeclaredColumnDefaultSql` and the local `nowColumnDefault` SQLite branch render for the DEFAULT, for `datetime`, `date` and `time` alike (the `time` CASE included). One statement, so SQLite fixes `'now'` once and every row and every column takes one instant. Existing rows taking the instant of the schema change is also what Postgres and MySQL give on `ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT now()`, so the dialects agree. The raw `UPDATE` does not touch `updated_at`.
- **A3. Scope of the UPDATE.** It runs only when the table was probed populated and only over columns absent from `existingColumns` as read before the `ALTER`, filtered by the same predicate that withheld the DEFAULT, so it names just-added columns only. A re-sync finds the column present and sends nothing: idempotent, no re-stamp. Both local `ADD COLUMN` doors (managed `initObjects` and `ensureShardTable`) and both remote doors (`syncSchema`, `syncSchemasBatch`) carry it; no third `createColumn` add door exists. `isSqlite` (in `createColumn`) and `dialectName === 'sqlite'` (in the rotation facet) are one answer (`dialectName` is derived from `isSqlite`), so the withhold and the backfill cannot disagree. The UPDATE has no `WHERE`: see S1.
- **A4. The differ arm and the emitter agree, so the local ceremony converges.** The arm fires for `sqlite`, a `NOW()` token, no physical DEFAULT, not multi-value; builtins and `formula` are skipped at the loop head. `createColumn` and `rebuildSqliteTablePatched` emit the `NOW()` DEFAULT for every such column (the scalar tail applies `applyDeclaredColumnDefault` to every non-multi-value type), and the emitted text reads back as an expression, never `none`. One rebuild therefore clears the entry; no local apply loop. Pinned by the new test's "drift is empty" after the ceremony.
- **A5. Category `safe` is right.** Main's rule for the class is "cannot lose data or fail on existing rows" (`isPublishedColumnChange` docblock: "a dropped or restated column DEFAULT"); the literal arm's `set_column_default` is `safe` on main and is applied on SQLite by the same rebuild. Adding a DEFAULT rewrites no row and cannot fail on one. `destructive` would be wrong in the other direction: the artifact-pinned boot gate refuses a boot for that category alone. No ADR in `docs/adr` fixes drift categories for column DEFAULTs (`set_column_default` appears in none; `autoMigrate` only in ADR-0062 and ADR-0120, on other subjects), so the code's own rule and the #36245 precedent govern. The unasked rebuild this implies is accepted as the category's existing meaning, with the disclosure owed in S2. Its doors, read in the code: dev boot under `autoMigrate: 'safe'` (`reconcileAndWarnDrift`, called from the same `initObjects` pass that just added the column; ignored under `NODE_ENV=production`), the publish of the object (`isPublishedColumnChange`), and the artifact-pinned boot gate (`runArtifactBootMigrationGate` applies every non-destructive entry, production included). The amendment's "no rebuild inside an additive sync" holds for the sync statement itself; under dev `autoMigrate: 'safe'` the same boot pass rebuilds right after it, for the DEFAULT only. Its governing text is about `storage.notNull`, which stays `destructive` and is not auto-applied.
- **A6. Wider reach of the arm.** It also reports any existing SQLite column whose field declares `NOW()` and which has no DEFAULT. On the local face that is a field that gained `NOW()` after its column existed (the additive sync never revisits a column); reporting it is correct, a gap main hid. On hosted Turso it is every `NOW()` column of every table the remote face created before #37345. There it is report-only: `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS.set_column_default` is `needs-table-rebuild`, the Turso config carries no `autoMigrate`, and the boot gate stands down on `driftReportCaveat`, so nothing is applied and nothing loops; `os migrate plan` lists the entries on every read until #37430 lands. See S3 for the carrier.
- **A7. Tests.** Local: `datetime` / `date` / `time` × nullable / `storage.notNull`, populated, through sync → drift → ceremony → later insert → empty drift, plus an empty-table control for all six. Remote: the same six through `syncSchema` and `syncSchemasBatch` and the local face in `turso-remote-not-null.test.ts` case 5, with the skipped entries and the `needs-table-rebuild` answers asserted; the parity file reads exactly one `set_column_default` per `NOW()` column on either differ. The assertions are ablation-sensitive on their face: a deleted backfill leaves `'null'`, which fails the shape regex and `not.toBeNull()`; a gated-off arm fails the exact `toEqual` on the op list. The dev reports four ablations red (local backfill, differ arm, each remote door); not re-run here. Gaps in S4.

- S1 (should-fix) — The `ADD COLUMN` and its backfill are not one atomic unit on three of the four doors, and a failure between them is never repaired. Local managed and shard doors: `knex.schema.alterTable(…)` then a separate `knex.raw(UPDATE)`, no transaction (SQLite DDL is transactional, so one `knex.transaction` would hold both). Remote `syncSchema`: one round trip per `ADD COLUMN`, then one more for the UPDATE. Only `syncSchemasBatch` is atomic (one `write` batch). If the UPDATE fails or never arrives (a dropped request on the hosted face, `SQLITE_BUSY`, a process stop), or a later `ADD COLUMN` of the same loop is refused, the `NOW()` column exists with NULL in every existing row; the next sync finds it in `existingColumns` and sends no backfill. For a nullable field nothing reports it (the drift is the same `set_column_default` either way); for `storage.notNull` the later tightening fails on the NULLs. The worst case equals what the remote face gave a nullable `NOW()` field before this PR, so it is not a regression, but the amended acceptance is "every existing row filled". Fix: one transaction locally; on remote `syncSchema`, the table's `ADD COLUMN`s and the backfill in one `write` batch, as the batch door already does. Same finding, second half: the UPDATE has no `IS NULL` guard, so on the non-atomic doors a row written with an explicit value between the `ADD COLUMN` and the UPDATE is overwritten with the sync instant; `col = COALESCE(col, expr)` closes it at no cost.
- S2 (should-fix) — The changeset discloses the wider report but not what `safe` does with it, and misstates the remedy for NOT NULL. Missing: (a) on a local SQLite database the new entry is applied unattended, by a full table rebuild, at a dev boot (`autoMigrate: 'safe'`), on publish of the object, and at an artifact-pinned boot, including for populated tables whose column predates this release; (b) `tighten_not_null` is `destructive`: `os migrate apply` alone does not impose it (`--allow-destructive` is needed; the changeset says "`os migrate apply` … gives the column its `NOW()` DEFAULT and the declared NOT NULL"), and an artifact-pinned boot on local SQLite is REFUSED while that entry stands, although the sync has just filled every row; (c) the PR body's worst-case line names an empty column or one extra to-do, not that refused boot. The final-head comment states (a) for the dev boot; the changeset, which is what ships to consumers, does not.
- S3 (should-fix, the seat's, not the diff's) — #37430 is named as carrier of the remote half, but its text carries less than this PR hands it. Its title, reach and acceptance speak of an edited or removed LITERAL default on a column the remote face created, and of `set_column_default` / `drop_column_default` only. This PR adds two things it does not name: an ABSENT `NOW()` DEFAULT (on columns added to a populated table, and on every pre-#37345 remote `NOW()` column), and `tighten_not_null` for the `storage.notNull` case, which a hosted environment now reaches where the sync used to refuse. One amendment comment on #37430 widening its acceptance to both makes the pointer in the changeset, the code comments and test case 5 true. Also for that card: the entry's message ends with `SAFE_COLUMN_REMEDY` ("publishing the object applies it … `os migrate apply`"), which is false on the remote face; `driftFindingWithoutRemedy` strips only the destructive remedy. Pre-existing for the literal arm, far more visible with this arm.
- S4 (should-fix) — Test gaps on paths this diff writes. (1) The shard door (`ensureShardTable`) backfill has no test and no ablation; it is a data-writing statement on its own call site. (2) The arm's wider reach, which the changeset announces, has no direct pin: a column that already exists with no DEFAULT under a `NOW()` field, never added in the test's own sync. (3) No negative control for the arm: a multi-value field declaring `NOW()`, and a column already carrying another expression, must report nothing. (4) The dev-boot path is unpinned: under `autoMigrate: 'safe'` one boot rebuilds, the next applies nothing (the no-loop claim of A4 through the door that actually auto-applies).
- N1 (nit) — `addsNotNullToPopulatedTable` now also answers for a `NOW()` DEFAULT; its name says NOT NULL only. The remote twin is already `addsRowSensitiveColumn`.
- N2 (nit) — Three places now quote an identifier by hand with the same rule (`sqliteNowBackfillSql`'s `quote`, `quoteRemoteIdentifier`, and the bare `"${table}"` in the remote DDL). Record only.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/driver-turso` is right. The level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone, `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3; same reading as record 7183095333 on PR #37425 and changeset `35872`). `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- M1 (must-fix) — `Clause-②: no` is wrong on both carriers; the line must read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset body and in the PR body. `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts` adds two named exports, `declaresSqliteNowColumnDefault` and `sqliteNowBackfillSql`, to the `.` entry of `@objectstack/driver-sql`, a published package (`publishConfig.access: public`, single entry `.` → `dist/index`). The clause's question is whether the card widens the accepted set or the public surface, and the public surface is what a package's built entry declarations reach (`execution-duties.md`). This is the same package, the same file, the same reason (the Turso remote face sharing one source) and the same seat as M1 of record 7182460866 on PR #37425, which was closed by exactly this correction; changeset `35872` is the earlier precedent. The final-head comment itself names the two exports "same reason and shape as #37345's three" and still declares `no`. The changeset must also name the two exports, as #37425's did; today it mentions neither. The level does not move: `yes (widening)` beside `Metadata-protocol: none` stays `patch`. The claim comment 7183611467 carries `Clause-②: no` as well; it predates the exports and is the seat's to note. Correcting the changeset moves the head, so this record does not carry over.
- Note on the other half of the line: the remote face accepting a `storage.notNull` `NOW()` field it used to refuse is a pull-back to the declared contract and would by itself be `no`; the exports alone decide `yes`.
- No `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner owed, no ADR-0087 marker owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev-report 7184726397: `open_questions` absent, nothing to answer. Its deviations: the differ arm and backfill are SQLite-only by design (accepted, A4: Postgres and MySQL take the expression DEFAULT on `ADD COLUMN`); the full dogfood battery not run (accepted, `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on the head); package-wide suites ran at `ce1140ae`, before the one main merge, with targeted re-runs at the head (accepted, `Test Core` 1–10 are green on `f83ae7cf`). Two local gates NOT MEASURED for environment reasons; CI ran them green.
- Final-head flag 1 (the `safe` arm also reports existing columns, and a dev boot rebuilds them): answered, A5 and A6; the category stands, the changeset owes the sentence (S2).
- Final-head flag 2 (two more `driver-sql` exports): answered, M1. The exports themselves are right; the declaration is not.
- Scope amendment 7183761626: the diff meets its replaced acceptance on the paths the tests drive. Two consequences of the route go to the seat for a decision, not to the dev: an artifact-pinned boot on local SQLite is refused after a `storage.notNull` `NOW()` field is added to a populated table, because `tighten_not_null` is unconditionally `destructive` even when the sync has just filled every row (S2 b); and #37430 must be widened to carry what this PR points at it (S3).
- Card acceptance line "case 5's remaining `NOW()` note is removed": done; case 5 is now one answer on both faces with the #37430 pointer.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5), every face: the backfill is one set-based `UPDATE` evaluated in the database, on both faces; no id materialisation, no row read into the application, no in-app join. The only added read is the existing bounded `SELECT 1 … LIMIT 1` probe, now also asked on the local face when a `NOW()` column is added on SQLite. No finding.
- Docs: no hand-written page states the populated `ADD COLUMN` rule for `NOW()` (the docs-drift comment is advisory and names pages through `syncSchema` only). Nothing owed.
- Escalated to the seat: S3 (amend #37430), and the boot-refusal consequence in S2 b.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37413-sqlite-now-default-populated`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `f83ae7cf7ea0ff4e9d2adfa6a5d7a66547cab0dc`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: contract record 7185397364 (declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`) reads **FAIL** on M1. The route holds: the backfill value is the DEFAULT's own expression, the `safe` category matches main's literal arm, no loop forms, and `patch` is right. M1 and S1, S2 and S4 close in this PR. S3 was the seat's to close, and it is now closed.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 10 files (+357/−75), `Fixes #37413`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch on `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/driver-turso`. `l1-face` is clean. Check-runs: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure.
2. **Premise**: SQLite refuses a non-constant DEFAULT on `ADD COLUMN` to a populated table. The PR adds the column nullable, backfills it with one set-based UPDATE, and reports the owed DEFAULT and NOT NULL. Locally a rebuild applies them; on the remote face a rebuild is needed (#37430). There is no SQL push-down question.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **M1.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on both carriers. `declaresSqliteNowColumnDefault` and `sqliteNowBackfillSql` are new exports of the published `@objectstack/driver-sql`, the same case as M1 on #37425. The changeset names both. The level stays `patch`.
   - **S1.** Make `ADD COLUMN` and the backfill atomic on every door. Today only `syncSchemasBatch` is atomic.
     - Locally, the managed door and the shard door each run inside one transaction.
     - On the remote side, `syncSchema` sends one `write` batch.
     - Guard the UPDATE (`WHERE col IS NULL`) so a row written in the gap is not overwritten.
   - **S2.** The changeset must state three behaviours plainly, and the PR body's worst-case line must say the same:
     - `autoMigrate: 'safe'` applies the new entry unattended by a full table rebuild on local SQLite. That happens at dev boot, on publish and at an artifact-pinned boot, including for `NOW()` columns that predate this release.
     - `tighten_not_null` needs `--allow-destructive`, not plain `os migrate apply`.
     - An artifact-pinned local boot is refused while `tighten_not_null` stands.
     The entry's remedy sentence must also not claim `os migrate apply` on the remote face.
   - **S4.** Add these tests:
     - the shard-door backfill, with an ablation;
     - a pre-existing `NOW()` column with no DEFAULT, which the changeset announces;
     - negative controls for the arm: a multi-value `NOW()` field, and a column already carrying an expression;
     - the `autoMigrate: 'safe'` path, where one boot rebuilds and the next applies nothing.
   - **S3: closed.** Scope amendment 7185412331 on #37430 now carries the remote half: the absent `NOW()` DEFAULT, including every pre-#37345 remote `NOW()` column, and `tighten_not_null`.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: these nits are fixed in the same push if cheap.
   - N1: `addsNotNullToPopulatedTable` now also answers for a `NOW()` DEFAULT, so its name is stale.
   - N2: identifier quoting is hand-rolled in three places.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: the remote rebuild is #37430 (amended 7185412331). The `'false'` differ drift stays on #37434.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier. Owed: M1, S1, S2 and S4 closed, a same-head delta PASS and an **ACCEPT**. Then the area lands it with `--land`.
